question: Should Reef core permanently own and release a Kubernetes/PostgreSQL relay alongside the Cloudflare relay, including the shared compatibility contract between both adapters?
rationale: The PR introduces a major supported deployment platform, persistent data model, operational release surface, and long-term two-adapter maintenance obligation that current main does not already establish.

options.title: Sponsor the portable relay
options.body: Approve the two-adapter direction, then require the image, proxy-trust, upgrade-safety, and real-runtime proof blockers to be resolved before merge.

options.title: Keep Kubernetes external
options.body: Retain Cloudflare as the core relay and publish the Node/PostgreSQL implementation as an externally maintained compatible deployment after confirming the required extension boundary.

options.title: Narrow the architecture first
options.body: Pause this branch and separately agree the relay-core/store contract before reviewing a Kubernetes runtime and chart.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the portable relay
recommendation.body: Approve the two-adapter direction, then require the image, proxy-trust, upgrade-safety, and real-runtime proof blockers to be resolved before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository design records Peter as the approver of Reef's architecture, and this choice changes that architecture's supported platform boundary.
